channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Tripadvisor Loan Soars as $600 Million Payment Boosts Confidence
item.description: Tripadvisor Inc.’s loan soared Monday as the company repaid $600 million of debt using proceeds of a sale, easing concerns for lenders as it faces a major leadership change and challenges from generative artificial intelligence tools.
item.dc:creator: Dorothy Ma and Katherine Schwartz

item.title: Big Take: All Eyes on Anthropic’s IPO
item.description: Anthropic’s IPO this week will be a bellwether for competitors like OpenAI and a signal of the AI industry’s health in the wake of the Nvidia scandal. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Asia Data Center Hotbed Hit by US Chip Curbs as Trump Visits
item.description: President Donald Trump is targeting Southeast Asia in Washington’s rush to tighten China’s access to the world’s most advanced chips, with his administration announcing new rules just before he travels to the region.
item.dc:creator: Ramsey Al-Rikabi and Philip J. Heijmans

item.title: Anthropic Faces a Longer Wait Than SpaceX to Join Stock Indexes
item.description: Anthropic’s planned initial public offering could generate billions of dollars in demand from index-tracking funds, though the artificial intelligence startup may have to wait longer than SpaceX did to join two major stock benchmarks.
item.dc:creator: Lu Wang

item.title: China’s Top AI Firms Limit Cyber Capabilities in Latest Models
item.description: China’s top AI developers are releasing advanced models with reduced offensive cyber capabilities, stifling their ability to aid online attacks following a government proposal to ban such technology from being exported.
item.dc:creator: Luz Ding and Mark Anderson

item.title: HSBC Sold $300 Million Troubled Data Center Loan at Discount
item.description: HSBC Holdings Plc offloaded a roughly $300 million piece of a loan to build a troubled New Mexico data center project at a steep discount, underscoring deepening anxiety surrounding the AI boom.
item.dc:creator: Reshmi Basu and Jeannine Amodeo

item.title: Nvidia Short Sellers Reap $24 Billion as Stock Extends Slide
item.description: Nvidia Corp.’s tumble in the wake of the scandal that led to former Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang’s ouster has fueled tens of billions of dollars in gains for short sellers.
item.dc:creator: Carmen Reinicke and Natalia Kniazhevich

item.title: Kalshi to Offer Stock Trading After Buying Brokerage
item.description: Kalshi Inc. is preparing to offer stock trading on its app after acquiring a brokerage firm called FB Securities. The company is trying to expand beyond just prediction markets. It will also offer exchange-traded funds. This story was first reported by the Wall Street Journal on Monday. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: MIT Brothers Cleared of Charges in $25 Million Crypto Case
item.description: Two brothers who graduated from Massachusetts Institute of Technology were cleared of charges that they stole $25 million in cryptocurrency, avoiding a new trial in the case after a jury failed to reach a verdict last year.
item.dc:creator: Bob Van Voris

item.title: Tradeweb Is Rolling Out AI Assistant for US Treasury Traders
item.description: Tradeweb Markets Inc. is launching an AI-powered assistant for government bond traders, as electronic-trading venues race to make artificial intelligence a central feature of their platforms.
item.dc:creator: Greg Ritchie

item.title: Trump, Duffy Deflect Responsibility for FAA Groundstop
item.description: Henry Harteveldt, president of Atmosphere Research Group, described Friday's total FAA groundstop that interrupted thousands of flights as, 'Humpty Dumpty falling off the wall, smashing into a billion bits and then being run over by a tank.' Harteveldt said that he gives airlines a lot of credit for working to get through the backlog, but said that the FAA has been 'starved' of funding by both Democratic and Republican administrations, including the first Trump Administration. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: What to Watch for in Nvidia Earnings
item.description: Nvidia is about to report earnings without Jensen Huang at the helm of the chipmaker. Colette Kress, the interim CEO will lead the call and certainly face questions about what direction she is taking the company in and how she will handle political and litigation risks. Bloomberg's Ed Ludlow reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Putin-Xi Meeting Unlikely to Bring Substantive Results for Trump, Says Jane Harman
item.description: Jane Harman, a former ranking Democrat on the House Intelligence Committee, talked about the potential national security risks from the Nvidia scandal, Trump’s upcoming meetings in Asia and the Senate Democratic leadership battle. Harman said that potential meetings between President Trump, Xi Jinping and Putin in China are unlikely to provide any substantive results other than a 'good photo op.' On the fight for Senate leadership between Chuck Schumer and Chris Van Hollen, Harman said that no matter the leader, Democrats should take seriously voters' calls for change. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Skilled Immigration Lowers Pay for College-Educated US Workers, Study Finds
item.description: Skilled immigration leads to lower wages for college-educated US workers, particularly in scientific fields, according to a paper by a Harvard University economist who served on President Donald Trump’s Council of Economic Advisers.
item.dc:creator: Aidan Williams

item.title: Microsoft Bug Undetected Since July Triggered Worldwide Outage
item.description: The bug that crippled Microsoft Corp. productivity software last week had been lurking undetected in the company’s data centers since July.
item.dc:creator: Matt Day

item.title: Hadrian Targets Critical Bottleneck in US Shipbuilding
item.description: Defense manufacturer Hadrian is investing $300 million to acquire and modernize a historic Pennsylvania foundry that produces critical components for US Navy ships and submarines. CEO Chris Power discusses why domestic casting capacity has become a major bottleneck for America’s defense industrial base and how AI and advanced manufacturing could boost production. He joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Tusk: Jensen Huang Should Not Return as Nvidia CEO
item.description: Tusk Ventures co-founder Bradley Tusk says Congress should examine the relationships between Nvidia’s former leadership and the Trump administration as questions remain over China, chip exports and national security. He discusses why he believes Jensen Huang should not return as CEO, what tighter US export controls could mean for Nvidia and the broader startup ecosystem, and why Silicon Valley’s reliance on high-profile founders and CEOs deserves more scrutiny as Anthropic prepares to go public. He joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Nvidia Fallout Adds New Tension to US-China AI Race
item.description: The US-China technology rivalry is in focus as President Trump travels to China for talks with Xi Jinping, with AI chips, export controls and rare earths among the key issues shaping the relationship. Krach Institute for Tech Diplomacy CEO Michelle Giuda discusses why Nvidia remains critical to US technological leadership and the importance of tightening chip export controls. She joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Nvidia Bull: AI Growth Story Remains Intact
item.description: I/O Fund CEO and lead tech analyst Beth Kindig says her long-term Nvidia bull case remains intact despite Jensen Huang’s departure, arguing the company could still reach a $20 trillion market value by 2030. She discusses why surging AI compute demand, Nvidia’s potential expansion into recurring software revenue and its lowest valuation multiple in years could support the stock - while AMD emerges as a more formidable competitor in rack-scale AI systems. She joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Nvidia’s Defining Week: CEO Search, Earnings and China
item.description: Bloomberg’s Ed Ludlow breaks down Nvidia's defining week as the chip giant searches for a new CEO while earnings loom. Plus, President Trump is set to meet with Xi and Putin in China, as AI chips, trade and the Nvidia fallout loom over the summit. And Anthropic prepares for a record-breaking IPO this week. (Source: Bloomberg)
